The load-bearing half of that oracle IS enforced: the second entry asserts `notes: "n2"`, which fails if notes are dropped. The auditor listed this under mutation-probe follow-ups, not among the three required edits, so I left the assertion byte-identical and flag it here for the probe.

tests.test: module shape: exports withAdvisoryLock as a function — apps/api/src/common/db-locks.spec.ts
tests.note: Verified by my own run (`npx jest src/common/db-locks.spec.ts --verbose`, 7 failed / 7 total): expected "function", received "undefined". Guarded `require` in the describe body, so module absence fails an assertion, not the import.

tests.test: (a) wait mode: SET / pg_advisory_lock / pg_advisory_unlock in order, release() with no arg, { acquired: true, value } — db-locks.spec.ts
tests.note: Expected {acquired:true,value:42}, received Symbol(db-locks not implemented) — the file's call-site sentinel keeps this on its own oracle instead of a TypeError. Note: the SQL-string equality assertions are white-box (they restate spec R1's prescribed query text), so they will break on any harmless wording change; T4 is the behavioral backstop.

tests.test: (b) fn rejecting still unlocks, releases the client with the error, and rethrows it — db-locks.spec.ts
tests.note: "Received promise resolved instead of rejected. Resolved to value: Symbol(db-locks not implemented)" — fails on the rejection oracle.

tests.test: (c) 55P03 on acquire → LockTimeoutError, fn never called, client released — db-locks.spec.ts
tests.note: rejects.toMatchObject({name:'LockTimeoutError'}) — resolved instead of rejected.

tests.test: (d) rejected connect() → LockUnavailableError before any lock query, fn never called — db-locks.spec.ts
tests.note: rejects.toMatchObject({name:'LockUnavailableError'}) — resolved instead of rejected.

tests.test: (e) try mode: failed acquire → { acquired: false }, no unlock, client released — db-locks.spec.ts
tests.note: Expected {acquired:false}, received the sentinel Symbol. This case was NOT in the runner output handed to me (it showed 5 blocks for 7 failures); I confirmed it by re-running the file.

tests.test: (f) waitMs 500 → SET lock_timeout = '500ms' — db-locks.spec.ts
tests.note: Expected ["SET lock_timeout = '500ms'"], received []. Also absent from the supplied runner output; confirmed by my re-run.

tests.test: T3-a mergeAllPendingForCustomer takes the lock before its first read — apps/api/src/orders/orders.merge-lock.spec.ts
tests.note: withAdvisoryLock called 0 times, expected 1. The stronger oracle (mockCallOrder === ['lock:cust-9','findMany']) is not reached yet but is sound: I confirmed orders.service.ts:815 and :1136 both start with `prisma.forTenant().order.findMany`, and prisma-mock.ts:220 has forTenant() return the same model surface, so the ledger will record 'findMany'.

tests.test: T3-b forceConsolidateCustomer takes the lock before its first read — orders.merge-lock.spec.ts
tests.note: Same: 0 calls, expected 1.

tests.test: T3-c mergeAllPendingForCustomer LockTimeoutError → 409 MERGE_IN_PROGRESS — orders.merge-lock.spec.ts
tests.note: caught === undefined, not an instance of ConflictException. Correct pre-state (nothing calls the throwing mock), but the payload oracle (code: 'MERGE_IN_PROGRESS') and `findMany` never-called assertion are never reached — see BEHAVIORAL blocker.

tests.test: T3-c forceConsolidateCustomer LockTimeoutError → 409 MERGE_IN_PROGRESS — orders.merge-lock.spec.ts
tests.note: Same shape: caught === undefined.

tests.test: T2 new-1 two concurrent merges go through the customer advisory lock (2 calls, family/key/mode/waitMs) — apps/api/src/orders/orders.scan-hardening.spec.ts
tests.note: Fails at line 1051: calls.toHaveLength(2), received 0. The preceding regression pin `expect(storeQty).toBe(15)` PASSES today (the in-process Map still serializes), so the failure is squarely on the new oracle. Strong test: asserts count AND every opts field.

tests.test: T2 new-2 LockTimeoutError → 409 MERGE_IN_PROGRESS — orders.scan-hardening.spec.ts
tests.note: caught === undefined, not ConflictException. Throws the class off the MOCKED module (dbLocks.LockTimeoutError), so the implementation's `instanceof` will match — good. Payload assertion unreached.

tests.test: T2 new-3 LockUnavailableError → 503 — orders.scan-hardening.spec.ts
tests.note: caught === undefined, not ServiceUnavailableException.

tests.test: T2 new-4 mergeLocksByOrder and withOrderMergeLock are gone — orders.scan-hardening.spec.ts
tests.note: Received `Map {}`, expected undefined — fails on its own value. Caveat: a purely negative structural assertion (a rename would satisfy it); new-1 is what makes it meaningful.

tests.test: T4 db-locks — real-Postgres contention: module shape + (a) same-key serialize + (b) different-key overlap + (c) waitMs timeout + (d) try on held key — apps/api/src/common/db-locks.db.spec.ts
tests.note: NOT covered by the supplied runner output; I ran `npm run local:test:db` against the running routeflow_postgres container: 5 failed / 1 passed / 6 total, the 1 pass being the pre-existing db-lane.db.spec.ts. All 5 T4 cases fail on assertions — module shape on typeof 'undefined', (a)/(b)/(d) on {acquired:'not-implemented'} vs the expected result object, (c) on waiterError undefined. The file's fallback stub invokes fn so the callback-synchronised cases can't hang. Flag: this lane is opt-in (RUN_DB_SPECS + jest.db.config.js) and is NOT part of `npm run test`, so R1's cross-process proof is not enforced by the default gate; it is also the only wall-clock-timing test in the change (300ms/500ms/1500ms budgets).

BEHAVIORAL: orders.scan-hardening.spec.ts T2 new-3 fails on `caught === undefined` — identical received value to new-2, so the red run does not distinguish ServiceUnavailableException from ConflictException; only the implementation run will.

BEHAVIORAL: orders.merge-lock.spec.ts T3-c (mergeAllPendingForCustomer) fails on `caught === undefined`; the `getResponse()` MERGE_IN_PROGRESS oracle and the `findMany` never-called oracle are both unreached at red time.

BEHAVIORAL: orders.merge-lock.spec.ts T3-c (forceConsolidateCustomer) — same as above; four tests across two files fail on the same undefined, proving the missing wiring rather than their own expected exception payloads.

BEHAVIORAL: R5's edit to the existing pin in orders.scan-hardening.spec.ts is still pending — the test at line 781 keeps its old title ('two concurrent merges on one instance serialize') and its SCOPE comment (lines 853-865) still states the mechanism is the controller-instance Map that new-4 asserts is deleted, so once R2 lands the file documents a mechanism it also proves is gone.
